title: Playing bass lines on guitar and learning from Jules Baptiste
summary: Jules Baptiste taught St. Cyr to play bass lines on guitar in small combos, which balanced the band; Bud Scott gave him a few tips.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Yeah, I never knew that. Well, I was going to ask a little more about the get back to New Orleans when you were young. One night you mentioned something about was it the bass player didn't show up when you were on the job, you began to play the ...
When you worked out your bass.

The thing about it is that Jules Batiste, he used the bass very much on the guitar, because they always played small combos. Like the fish fry there was two pieces at the Morris, and the guitar just strumming rhythm was much of a support. That bass gave it more of a sound support. And Jules specialized in the bass. And I adopted that style from him, in fact I had taken lessons from him and I adopted his style of playing. And most of the small jobs, as I said before, Piron used to give me, were just small combos, maybe four pieces. And we used the strongest instrumentation for those four pieces. We used violin, trumpet, and clarinet, and guitar. Well we would use the bass player. See I played enough bass on the guitar to balance the band.
Almost like the piano left hand. Exactly.
That's how you worked out that style. That's how you worked out that style.
That's right. That's right. That's right. Yeah.

Sometime we'd use the trumpet and trombone and eliminate the clarinet. That was a good power there. For the dancers still had a good accompaniment with the guitar using the bass. Yeah. Is there any other guitar player that you sort of tried to pattern your style or influence
to more than others that you loved?
